title: Reaction Kinetics
description: How fast a reaction goes: the rate constant k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT) of Arrhenius, roughly doubling every ten degrees. Unlocks the Air Separation Unit and hydrogen from coal and steam.

puzzle.goal: A reaction has activation energy E. Write how many times faster r it goes at temperature U than at T, with the gas constant R, if its rate constant is A·e^(−E/RT).
puzzle.name: Arrhenius ratio
puzzle.ask: Find r for E = @{E} J/mol, R = 8.314 J/(mol·K), T = @{T} K and U = @{U} K.
puzzle.method: k = A·e^(−E/RT) at each temperature; the A cancels in the ratio.
